symptom: Field test on ako/mxcli#2104 (and ako/mxcli#2063): a `test --attach` run with a test that had to be built, or a `test --local` run, made the project's `run --local --watch` dev loop rebuild (the first build failing) and apply by restarting the runtime, dropping every browser session including a --hub preview; on the spike app the restart itself failed with EOFException. The attach's own message said the app's serve process was left alone.
cause: Both write the test microflows into the same .mpr the dev loop watches. The attach used a serve process of its own for its build, but the watcher saw the model change, and then the cleanup, as edits. --attach also never restored the .mpr byte for byte (only --local did), so even after cleanup the model differed.
file: cmd/mxcli/docker/watchhold.go (HoldWatch/ReleaseWatch, ModelDigest, watchHoldGate), cmd/mxcli/docker/runlocal.go (the watcher consults the gate), cmd/mxcli/docker/runstate.go (HeldBy, Covered), cmd/mxcli/testrunner/runner_attach.go and runner.go (hold + snapshot restore), cmd/mxcli/cmd_run_lifecycle.go (status shows the hold)
insight: Two processes writing one project need a protocol, not a better watcher heuristic: the writer announces itself and the watcher decides on release by content, not mtimes. The release check needs the project put back byte for byte, which test --local already did (projectSnapshot) and --attach did not. Moving the watcher's baseline is not enough on its own: the run state's Last.Source must move with it, or `run status` and `run wait` see a pending change no build will cover. The control: with the hold disabled three gate tests fail; on the spike app main's binary rebuilt twice for one test --local run (restart failed) and once for a mixed attach run, the fixed binary built nothing and an edit afterwards still built.
